correctness.rationale: An explicit two/three-letter alternating bridge proves strong connectivity; duplicating the specified nonfully alternating edges balances every original constrained vertex. The Eulerian tour gives the exact upper length; a potential on all 2^(n-1) binary vertices bounds the increment of every possible supplementary edge by one and forces precisely 2F_(n-1)-2 extras even if forbidden windows are allowed. The counting bijection gives the same number of duplicated edges. Standard-library verification of degrees, actual tours and all binary-edge inequalities at n=3..16 returned VERIFY_OK. A separate Hungarian min-cost postman checker n=3..13 returned CROSSCHECK_OK. No finite test substitutes for the quantified proof.

value.rationale: Maximum constant run length two is a standard symmetric binary constrained language, while covering every finite admissible factor (including transient factors not periodic on their own) is a naturally stronger objective than exact-once constrained de Bruijn sequencing. An exact all-order circular covering length, the sharp unavoidable overhead 2F_(n-1)-2, a forbidden-free optimal tour, and a uniform global dual certificate resolve a motivated information/word-combinatorial invariant; this is not a parameter renaming, known-table recomputation, or isolated numerical increment.
